STEP 1 - Scene: This is a small portion of roasted sweet potato pieces on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square white dish roughly 26 cm across its longest diagonal-free edge; I'll take it as a side plate of about 22 cm width. Area ≈ 22 x 22 x ~0.85 (rounded square corners) ≈ 410 cm^2. The food sits in the centre-left, and no other food is part of the meal.

STEP 3 - Items: Five pieces of roasted sweet potato (orange flesh with browned, caramelised skin edges). No visible oil or sauce beyond a light glaze.

STEP 4 - Area: Each piece is roughly 3 x 2.5 cm footprint (about 6–8 cm^2 each, the larger ones about 8 cm^2). Total food footprint ≈ 5 pieces x 7 cm^2 ≈ 35 cm^2, about 9% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pieces are about 2–2.5 cm tall, roughly cube-like chunks. Each piece ≈ 3 x 2.5 x 2 cm ≈ 15 cm^3 (about 12 ml after accounting for rounded faces). Five pieces ≈ 60 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut vegetable pieces, bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 60 ml x 0.6 ≈ 36 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted sweet potato ≈ 90 kcal/100 g (cooked, no added fat). 36 g x 0.90 ≈ 32 kcal. Allowing for a light glaze or oil, add ~2 g of oil at 880 kcal/100 g ≈ 18 kcal, giving about 50 kcal total.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Five bite-sized pieces of sweet potato on a large plate is a small snack-sized portion. About 36–40 g and roughly 35–50 kcal is plausible for what is visible.

Sweet potato total: 36 g, ~90 kcal/100 g → ~32 kcal. Light oil/glaze: ~2 g → ~18 kcal.
